section_title: Can ancient hostility make the Philistines’ revenge right?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 15 This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because the Philistines acted in vengeance, taking vengeance with malice of soul to destroy Judah with ancient hostility, 16 therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I will stretch out My hand against the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the coast. 17 I will execute great vengeance against them with furious reproof. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I lay My vengeance upon them.’”

context_lines: The final announcement in the chapter concerns the Philistines. Their old hostility has become a malicious desire to destroy Judah.

The Lord will stretch out His hand against them, cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the coast. [Brown–Driver–Briggs](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/3774.htm) identifies Cherethites as a name for the Philistines or a part of them; the verse is not introducing an unrelated enemy.
The chapter ends as its earlier announcements have: the people will know that He is the Lord when His judgment comes. Longstanding hatred supplies the accusation, not a justification for the revenge.
common_interpretation_lines: [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ezekiel/25.htm) reads stored-up hatred and the search for an opportunity to act on it as accumulating guilt before God. [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/ezekiel/25.htm) understands the announcement as directed against Israel’s hostile coastal neighbors.
The chapter has confronted contempt, dismissive pride and revenge. Its closing announcement shows that a grievance carried for generations still answers to the Lord.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
